body.hook: When a Chinese speaker says someone is 画蛇添足 huà shé tiān zú, "drawing legs on a snake," they mean the person ruined something by doing too much. These four-character idioms, 成语 chéngyǔ, come from stories over 2,000 years old and are still used every day.

vocabulary.definition: Four-character idiom, usually from a classical story.
The classical story or source behind an idiom.

vocabulary.term: 画蛇添足 huà shé tiān zú
vocabulary.definition: Draw a snake and add feet: ruin something by overdoing it.

vocabulary.term: 守株待兔 shǒu zhū dài tù
vocabulary.definition: Guard a tree stump waiting for rabbits: wait for luck instead of working.

vocabulary.term: 对牛弹琴 duì niú tán qín
vocabulary.definition: Play the zither to a cow: speak to the wrong audience.

study.title: 成语故事 Chéngyǔ gùshi
study.question: What stories lie behind Chinese idioms, and how are they used?
study.passage:
Story 1, 画蛇添足 (from an ancient text, about 2,000 years old): Some servants had one jug of wine. They agreed that whoever drew a snake first would drink it. One man finished first, picked up the wine and said, "I can even add feet!" While he drew feet, another man finished his snake, took the wine and said, "Snakes don't have feet. Yours isn't a snake!" and drank it. Meaning: doing something unnecessary that spoils the result.
Story 2, 守株待兔 (from the philosopher Hán Fēizǐ): A farmer saw a rabbit run into a tree stump and die. He took it home and ate it. From then on, he stopped farming and waited by the stump for another rabbit. None came, and his fields were ruined. Meaning: relying on luck instead of effort.
Story 3, 对牛弹琴: A musician played beautiful music to a cow, but the cow kept eating grass. Meaning: talking about something to an audience that can't understand or appreciate it.
Using chéngyǔ: 你的作文已经很好了，别画蛇添足。Nǐ de zuòwén yǐjīng hěn hǎo le, bié huà shé tiān zú. = Your essay is already good; don't overdo it. 想考好成绩不能守株待兔，要努力学习。
Task: Retell one story in Mandarin in six sentences, then write two sentences using each chéngyǔ in modern situations.
